# Official historical payload evidence matrix

This directory contains public metadata and source comparison inputs. It contains no installed-payload identity, reviewed production policy, signer private key, or installer binary. A passing fixture does not admit an installer into production.

## Exact scope

The `Historical payload evidence` workflow is restricted to same-repository PRs from `feat/unified-workspace-ux` into `feat/native-cli-finalization` that change the dedicated fixture/workflow/provenance paths. It checks out and verifies the event’s exact head SHA. Optional later manual dispatch requires a reviewed 40-character source SHA. Other existing workflows can still run on that push; they use separate VMs and do not execute these ignored installer entrypoints. Exactly nine fixed versions (`0.14.0`, `0.15.0`, `0.16.0`, `0.17.0`, `0.17.1`, `0.17.2`, `0.17.5`, `0.17.6`, `0.17.7`) each have `clean` and `seeded-existing` cases, for **18 separate disposable Windows 2022 VMs**. Every job compiles its own test executable from the exact reviewed checkout; no executable transfer or shared fixture-state optimization is used. No runner cache/profile is reused and no ordinary Rust test or application startup precedes the initial absence check. Build preparation and compilation happen first. Do not run the ignored entrypoints on a user's computer or general-purpose development VM.

The test controller creates only a temporary same-user restricted token with `LUA_TOKEN | DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE`. It records the parent and candidate token. The gate requires the same SID/session, false elevation, medium integrity, no enabled administrator SID, and no privilege other than change-notify. When this newly created restricted token differs only by High integrity, the test-only owner may lower that token to Medium using `SetTokenInformation(TokenIntegrityLevel)` before process creation. Its only constructor creates the restricted token; it cannot accept a caller-supplied token handle. The parent handle closes before this one-shot operation. Actual readback must equal the requested label-only change, the parent observation must remain unchanged, and all eligibility predicates must pass. Error/unknown outcomes block without replay and preserve before/after diagnostics. Other integrity levels or eligibility failures are rejected. The controller then creates only the exact worker test, suspended, checks its actual token again, puts that fixture worker in a kill-on-close job, records its exact process identity, and resumes once. It never changes parent/system tokens, UAC, accounts, passwords or security policies, and never uses `SANDBOX_INERT`. These are test-only helpers; production does not manipulate tokens.

The worker repeats the token check, positively checks absent Desk data/install locations, six registration slots in both registry views and hives, relevant shortcuts, matching machine/WiX registration, and matching running Desk processes. Process-name observation is a fixture refusal check, not production quiescence authority. It requires both existing WebView registration and a successful WebView loader version lookup, without starting a browser or downloading a prerequisite.

The worker uses the production official catalog, bounded asset transport, preparation service and committed Minisign key. `catalog.json` is a compiled, closed nine-version evidence catalog, derived exactly from `../version-history-releases.json`. Each entry fixes the complete release identity and both Windows installer/signature tuples, including IDs, names, sizes, hashes, URLs and creation/update timestamps. The release source remains a bounded live official read and must match before and after preparation. Unknown versions, cases, mixed installer/signature pairs, malformed provenance, source SHA mismatch and cross-version/case/run records stop before fixture effects. No downloaded manifest can add a version or expectation.

The controller freezes one version, one `clean`/`seeded-existing` case, exact fixture source SHA, compiled `CC_DESK_BUILD_SHA`, run ID and attempt before creating the evidence root or restricted worker. Requested and compiled source SHAs must match. A create-new `fixture-binding.json` is compared with the worker's independently frozen binding before token observation, package preparation or seeding, again around both release identity checks, and before installer effects and final acceptance of the observation. The evidence root and artifact name include version, case, run ID and attempt. Existing raw token, inventory, registry, shortcut and process receipts keep their original shapes.

Binding records distinguish `fixtureSourceCommit`/`compiledSourceCommit` from the historical `releaseSourceCommit`. `fixtureCatalogSha256` hashes the exact compiled catalog bytes, which are retained as `fixture-catalog.json`; `releaseCatalogSha256` hashes the committed full release fixture; scoped `.gitattributes` rules disable text conversion for these hash-bound inputs on Windows; `fixtureFingerprint` hashes the selected typed fixture serialized by `serde_json::to_vec` (including its complete selected tuple and provenance). Before/after selected-identity reports and final review receipts repeat the same binding. This is provenance for an observation, never automatic policy import.

The service retains the original verified package and copies exact verified bytes into a create-new executable; a no-write/no-delete pinned file handle stays held through process consumption. The fixed 0.17.7 installer remains asset 576637999 (4,966,193 bytes, SHA256 `e9ffbc5ba627f0c133a4385db404342a7344729339185e6f9b8ee6b5969086ac`) with signature 576637991 (420 bytes, SHA256 `30b26f21c76d8c30bf4ca042ff699f1dd5d181af54f0e8956a3bff10650b80e2`); all other exact tuples are in the catalog.

Only production `CommandLine::nsis` and `PreparedProcess` execute the installer: explicit application, `/S /UPDATE /NS`, final unquoted `/D=` path containing spaces and Chinese characters, no `/R`, a private installer job, durable launch/identity/resume records, actual installer token verification, bounded terminal wait and observed empty job. No historical app or uninstaller is explicitly launched. Failures are not retried and fixture state is not cleaned up by guessing.

The seeded case creates only fresh fixture-owned old registration, old-target shortcuts, a never-executed `Old Desk.exe` placeholder, and a source-only leftover. It measures old-binary deletion, `/NS` shortcut migration, `/UPDATE` leftover retention, overwriting CC Desk Explorer values and deletion of both legacy cc-box Explorer trees. The clean case alone cannot establish these behaviors.

## Evidence and limits

Artifacts retain token/environment/process/command receipts, the exact official installer and signature, raw typed registry/security snapshots, raw known shortcuts, installed PE identity and a complete bounded installed-tree inventory with file identities, attributes, owner/DACL descriptors, sizes and SHA256. Raw installed files are copied into the artifact area only after a complete regular-file inventory and a second held-object/digest comparison. Upload paths exclude the live install and package-store trees, so unsupported/reparse objects are not recursively uploaded. Evidence remains available after failure wherever capture was possible.

Budgets are explicit: 120-second installer wait, 300-second worker wait, 256 tree entries/16 levels, 256 MiB per file/512 MiB total payload, 4 MiB per report, 64 registry nodes across a phase, 32 values/subkeys per node, 4 KiB per registry value, 64 KiB per descriptor or shortcut, 4,096 machine uninstall keys and 16,384 process entries. Inventory overflow and unsupported objects are blockers, not truncation success.

Source comparison inputs pin each tagged config's exact bytes, historical commit and immutable URL, the common identical installer hook, and the Tauri 2.10.1 NSIS template. Each source commit's observed package-lock SHA and locked CLI version are recorded; those lock hashes are source provenance, not downloaded installer-byte attestation. The older eight tags explicitly lack `tauri.windows.conf.json` and declare no bundled resources. Their only accepted tree shape is the root, `cc-desk.exe` and `uninstall.exe`. Version 0.17.7 additionally requires its existing exact-size/hash ConPTY DLL, OpenConsole executable and license. Both shapes require the selected exact x64 PE product/file version. Seeded cases additionally retain unchanged `source-only-leftover.txt` and reject a retained `Old Desk.exe`. Complete enumeration, unknown-path rejection, native token/job checks, pinned byte verification and known-effect checks are unchanged. No old executable or generated uninstaller hash is guessed; measured bytes must be reviewed independently for each version/case. The defaults are documented upstream at `https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/tauri-cli-v2.10.1/crates/tauri-utils/src/config.rs`. Those sources do not independently attest that arbitrary signed bytes were compiled with that exact contract. The fixture does not claim a whole-system effect trace, deterministic generated uninstaller bytes, correct data switching, rollback, shared-current-data compatibility, or a successful real return. Independent review must compare each version's clean and seeded outputs and decide separately whether a narrowly keyed policy is justified. `payload_policy.rs`, its `REVIEWED` table, `SUPPORTED_ROUNDTRIP_ENABLED=false` and `acceptance.rs` are untouched by this matrix expansion. Unknowns remain blockers to that later admission.

Local checks: `node --test tests/scripts/historyPayloadFixture.node.mjs`; Windows test registration and `Win32_UI_Shell`, `Win32_Globalization`, `Win32_System_Diagnostics_ToolHelp` features are required. The controller entrypoint is `tests::version_history_payload::HistoryPayload_Controller_001`, ignored by the ordinary suite. Pure metadata/token rejection tests remain independent of installer execution. `HistoryPayload_FixtureCatalog_020`, `FixtureMutation_021`, `Binding_022`, `BindingRecord_023` and `InventoryMatrix_024` cover the fixed matrix and malformed/mixed binding/shape rejection. The dedicated workflow runs only these selected pure contracts before the ignored controller; no ordinary application startup or broad native test suite is added to observation VMs. Rust compilation, actual restricted-token viability and installation evidence were NOT RUN during Linux authoring.


## Validation status of the matrix expansion

The portable Node contracts cover observed red/green changes; they verify committed tuples, snapshot hashes, source-level binding guards, the 18-job workflow and shared NSIS-template provenance. They do not execute Rust or certify Windows behavior. The nine-version matrix has not been run during Linux authoring, and no newer measured payload evidence or production admission is claimed. Windows compilation, Rust contract execution, actual restricted-token execution and all 18 final bound observation reports remain required after independent source review. Existing 0.17.7 measurements are historical evidence, not results for this new fixture source.
